title: Deployable POC Playlist and Constraints Log
content:
Purpose and audience:
- Quick-run notebook for SEs running customer POCs that must be deployable to Dedicated or Private later. Primary audience: solutions engineers, customer SREs, onboarding PMs.

High-level objective:
- Deliver a reproducible, low-friction POC that verifies latency (p50/p95/p99), cost envelope, and integration touchpoints within 2–3 weeks, with clear gating to move to a Dedicated capacity pilot.

Scope (what this doc covers):
- Week-by-week sprint playlist (tasks + owners)
- Hard constraints and non-negotiables from infra/compliance
- Workshop agenda and artifacts to collect from customer
- Acceptance criteria and rollback policies
- Quick checklist for the final demo and handoff

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep the first workshop under 90 minutes. Too many stakeholders = no decisions.
- Prioritize a simple echo workflow to validate networking first (webhook -> Redwood hosted -> callback).
- If customer asks for >32k context, flag with infra early — might need Dedicated with different kernel profile.

Week 0: Pre-engagement (2–4 business days)
- Draft SOW + success metrics template (owner: Maya) — use minimal legal language, customer signature optional for trial creds.
- Collect data sample (owner: customer success / Rita) — 200 representative prompts + 50 long-context docs.
- Environment checklist: customer VPC peering? VPN? SSH bastion? (owner: Benji)
- Create tracking board: JIRA ticket JIRA-SEA-1287 and a shared Google sheet for cost estimates.

Workshop A: Kickoff (Day 0, 60–90m)
- Attendees: SE, customer PO, 1 SRE, 1 security contact, product manager (optional).
- Agenda: intro goals (5m), success metrics alignment (10m), data walk-through (20m), demo of minimal pipeline (10m), integration constraints and network mapping (15m), next steps & T-shirt sizing (10m).
- Artifacts to collect: example prompts, schema for input/output, list of internal SLAs (target p99), compliance checklist (PII?), sample traffic patterns (requests/sec, typical token counts).

Week 1: Lab and integration (days 1–7)
- Task: Provision sandbox environment (hosted trial credentials OR customer sandbox on Private) (owner: Benji)
- Task: Implement webhook PoC that sends 10 requests/sec burst, sample response logging (owner: Samir)
content_2:
- Task: Run baseline perf on candidate models (owner: Ethan) — record p50/p95/p99 for small, medium, large contexts
- Deliverable: short perf report (1 page) with clear recommendation (e.g., gptx-small quantized for cost-sensitive, gptx-medium for quality).

Week 2: Quality + gating (days 8–14)
- Create prompt set of 50 golden prompts and 30 edge cases (owner: SE + customer PO)
- Run automated eval harness (owner: Ethan) - compare to baseline responses, record fail rates and hallucination examples
- Workshop B (mid-week): Review eval results with customer, align on acceptable error rates, discussion of fallback behavior for timeouts or high-latency responses.

Hard constraints log (must-check):
- Networking: outbound egress allowed to api.redwood.ai endpoints or explicit subnet for Private.
- Data residency: if customer requires EU-only, we must select EU region; Dedicated requires SLA negotiation.
- Token budget: customer committed daily token cap? (if yes, configure quota rules)
- Model hosting: some enterprise customers disallow external third-party models — need to offer Redwood-verified open models or Dedicated with pinned model artifacts.
- Hardware: If target throughput >200 rps with <150ms p95, need multi-GPU partitioning and batching — escalate to platform-eng.

Risk register (quick):
- Risk: Data contains PII; Mitigation: enable KMS and ensure logs masked (owner: Rita).
- Risk: Network egress blocked; Mitigation: provide ip-range list and test with customer networking team (owner: Benji).
- Risk: Eval shows unacceptable hallucination on legal prompts; Mitigation: design constrained prompt + reranker fallback or label as not supported (owner: Ethan + customer PO).

Acceptance criteria to graduate to Dedicated pilot (all must be met):
- Latency: p95 <= customer SLO (usually 250–500ms depending on context length) under baseline traffic pattern.
- Reliability: error rate <0.5% during a 24h soak test at expected load.
- Quality: automated eval fail rate <= X% (define with customer in workshop B).
- Integration: secure network path established and test webhook callback success >= 99% for 1k messages.
- Cost estimate: unit token cost within agreed envelope + projected monthly spend for pilot signed off.

Canary and rollback checklist (short):
- Canary config: 5% traffic to Dedicated, 95% to hosted fallback, 30-minute soak with alerting on any SLO breach.
- Rollback trigger: p95 jump > 2x baseline OR error rate > 1% sustained > 5min.
- Rollback action: switch routing policy back to hosted variant + escalate to on-call eng.

Workshop artifacts (what to save to Drive):
- network-mapping.png (screenshot from customer diagram)
- sample-prompt-set.csv (golden prompts with expected outputs)
- perf-report-onepage.pdf (from Week 1)
content_3:
Demo run script (for SE):
- Step 0: confirm sandbox creds + environment variables set (REDBOX_API_KEY, REGION override)
- Step 1: fetch sample prompt file and run local runner: python run_poc.py --inputs sample-prompt-set.csv --out results.json
- Step 2: run perf harness: ./perf-run --rps 50 --model gptx-small --context 2k --duration 300s
- Step 3: collect logs: curl https://logs.redwood.internal/poctest?run_id=XXX --auth <token>
- Step 4: share results in Slack thread and schedule Workshop B if gating criteria unmet.

Handoff checklist for SE -> Customer Success / Onboarding (when POC completes):
- Final report with metrics and artifacts uploaded to Drive (owner: Maya)
- Shared runbook + escalation list (owner: Benji)
- Billing estimate and uplift guidance for Dedicated (owner: finance contact)
- Open JIRA for any product changes required for production (owner: product engineer)

Open questions (to resolve in next sync):
- Do we need to support HC encryption with a particular HSM vendor? Customer mentioned "Vault by V" — add to security run.
- Will customer traffic pattern include sustained 24/7 bursts (not just office hours)? If yes, need to change autoscaling policy defaults.
- Is there a compliance requirement for message retention < 30 days? If so, configure log retention and S3 lifecycle.

Action items (short list):
- Maya: finalize SOW template and push to shared Drive (due 2024-11-10).
- Benji: provide network IP allowlist and test script (due 2024-11-12).
- Ethan: perf report draft v0 (due 2024-11-14).
- Rita: confirm PII handling with customer security and redact training data where needed (due 2024-11-13).

Quick raw notes from Kickoff (copied):
- Customer cares most about predictable token cost and avoiding spikes during end-of-quarter batch jobs.
- They use an internal retriever that returns doc IDs with metadata — need to confirm output schema and field names.
- Security team: "no logs retained longer than 45 days, audit trail required for all model calls".

Appendix: Useful commands and artifacts
- Perf harness repo: github.com/redwood-inference/poc-perf (branch: maya/small-run)
- Model selection cheat-sheet: models/redwood-verified.md
- Network allowlist: 34.118.0.0/16, 35.202.0.0/16 (add region-specific ranges)

End of doc.

(Version notes: this is intentionally conversational and checklist-first so SEs can copy-paste sections into emails and workshop slides.)
